project: Automatos AI — PRD-246 Studio on mobile (the compact form of the design system)
description: Give every Studio surface a compact form so a phone gets the design system rather than the hybrid it gets today (Studio chrome + Studio tokens + classic bodies). Spec: docs/PRDS/PRD-246-STUDIO-MOBILE.md — decisions M1-M8 are LOCKED. Base is `studio`, NEVER `main`: prod is frozen until Gerard signs both the desktop pass and the phone pass. Build order matters: US-007 flips the route forks and must be last.

userStories.title: Foundations: the compact conventions, safe area and touch targets
userStories.description: Establish where compact rules live and the primitives every later story reuses. (a) In app/globals.css add ONE clearly-commented '── Studio compact (< 1024) ──' region inside @layer components, after the chrome guard, where every surface's compact rules go; later stories append there, they do not scatter @media blocks. (b) The Studio shell and any bottom-anchored Studio surface respect env(safe-area-inset-bottom) — reuse the existing .safe-bottom helper (globals.css ~:3034), do not invent a second one. (c) Every Studio control that is a tap target (.sh-item, .cc-tab, .cc-btn, .cc-filter-pill, .cc-seg button) is at least 44px high under 768px. (d) .md-view defaults to its compact density under 768px (the desktop rules stay). No surface layout changes in this story.
acceptanceCriteria: A '── Studio compact' region exists in app/globals.css inside @layer components, after the chrome-guard block, with a comment naming it as the home for compact rules. → DONE — frontend/app/globals.css:2962 '── Studio compact (< 1024)' banner inside @layer components, after the chrome guard (:2856), closed by :3018 'end of the compact region'; gate components/__tests__/studio-mobile-scope.test.ts asserts exactly one banner + position.

components/layout/main-layout.tsx (or the Studio shell markup it renders) applies .safe-bottom (or env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) to the mobile sheet and the shell's bottom edge; no second safe-area helper is introduced (grep: exactly one 'safe-area-inset-bottom' definition). → DONE — frontend/components/layout/main-layout.tsx:96 `className="sh-shell safe-bottom"` (shell bottom edge, 100dvh + border-box) and :154 the Studio branch of the mobile SheetContent carries `safe-bottom`; grep 'safe-area-inset-bottom' globals.css = 2 hits, both the one .safe-bottom helper at :3093.

A media query under 768px raises .sh-item, .cc-tab, .cc-btn, .cc-filter-pill and .cc-seg button to min-height 44px. → DONE — globals.css:2992-3002 one rule inside @media (max-width: 767px) raises .sh-item, .cc-tab, .cc-filter-pill, .cc-btn and .cc-seg button to min-height: 44px; the rail also gets 44px + thumb metrics across the whole compact band (:2982, max-width: 1023px, where it lives in a sheet).

A media query under 768px applies the .md-view-compact metrics to .md-view (font-size and block spacing), without changing the desktop rules. → DONE — globals.css:3009-3015 inside @media (max-width: 767px): .md-view takes .md-view-compact's metrics (12.5px/1.55, 0.7em block gap, 1.15em head gap, h1 1.125rem, h2 1rem, h3/h4 0.9375rem). Desktop .md-view (14px/1.65) and .md-view-compact are byte-unchanged.

cd frontend && npm run test -- components/shared/__tests__/markdown-typography.test.ts app/__tests__/page-frames.test.ts → green (the desktop guards are untouched). → DONE — npm run test -- components/shared/__tests__/markdown-typography.test.ts app/__tests__/page-frames.test.ts → 2 files, 8 tests passed. Full suite 151 files / 778 tests green.
userStories.notes: The chrome guard added in the PRD-244 review lives just above; do NOT remove or weaken it — a compact rule must never give a chrome row flex-shrink: 1.

userStories.title: Command Centre compact
userStories.description: The Command Centre reads on a phone. Tabs (.cc-tabs) scroll horizontally with the active tab scrolled into view on mount; .cc-stats goes 2-up under 768; .cc-sum-grid is already 1-up at 1199 — verify and keep; the board (.cc-kb-grid) keeps one row per status and gains scroll-snap with a sticky .cc-kb-head; the activity view uses its card density under 768 (the table is desktop-only); the calendar offers month/day rather than a shrunken grid. CSS in the compact region wherever possible; touch components only where behaviour (scroll-into-view, density default) demands it.
acceptanceCriteria: Under 768px .cc-stats is 2 columns and .cc-tabs scrolls horizontally without clipping the active tab; a test asserts the rules exist in the compact region. → DONE — globals.css:3025-3026 (@media max-width: 767px, compact region) .cc-stats → repeat(2, minmax(0,1fr)); the old 700px step is DELETED (:1624) so the boundary is 768, not beside it. :3021-3022 the page gutter comes in to 16px and .cc-tabs' negative bleed comes in WITH it — .cc-page sets overflow-y: auto, which computes overflow-x: auto, so a -28px bleed inside a 16px gutter was 12px of sideways page scroll clipping the strip. .cc-tabs keeps its desktop overflow-x: auto. Asserted: components/__tests__/studio-mobile-scope.test.ts 'Command Centre: the gutter, the tab strip, the stats and the board'.

The active .cc-tab is scrolled into view when the Command Centre mounts on a narrow viewport (component behaviour, asserted with a mocked width). → DONE — new hooks/use-tab-strip-scroll.ts (ONE hook for every Studio strip, US-002/004/005/006) scrolls .cc-tab.active into view with {block:'nearest',inline:'center'} when useIsTabletOrBelow(); wired at components/command-center/command-center-shell.tsx:115 + :204 (ref on nav.cc-tabs). Test components/command-center/__tests__/cc-compact.test.tsx 'scrolls the active tab into view on a compact viewport' (width mocked via @/hooks/use-mobile, ?tab=governance = 7th of 7) and the desktop counterpart asserting it does NOT fire.

The board keeps grid-auto-flow: column with scroll-snap under 768px and .cc-kb-head is sticky within its column; the chrome guard still lists .cc-kb-head. → DONE — globals.css:3031-3043: .cc-kb-grid keeps grid-auto-flow: column (desktop rule at :1898, unchanged) and adds grid-auto-columns: minmax(84%,1fr) + scroll-snap-type: x mandatory; .cc-kb-col gets scroll-snap-align: start and becomes its own scroller (overflow: hidden auto) so :3042 .cc-kb-head { position: sticky; top: 0 } actually sticks — the head is a sibling of .cc-kb-body, so sticky needs the COLUMN to be the scroll container; .cc-kb-body then sizes to content. The chrome guard (:2868) still lists .cc-kb-head and still gives it flex-shrink: 0 — unchanged, and page-frames.test.ts is green.

components/command-center/activity-tab.tsx defaults to its card density (not the table) when useIsMobile() is true, with a test. → DONE — components/command-center/activity-tab.tsx:148-152: the four-column table is desktop-only — const density = isPhone ? 'cards' : preferred, and :186 the Density .cc-seg is not rendered at all on a phone rather than offering a view that cannot be read at 390px. Test cc-compact.test.tsx 'a phone gets the cards and is not offered the density toggle' + the desktop counterpart. Same treatment for the calendar (calendar-tab.tsx:467-472): a 60px+repeat(7,1fr) week is 47px/day at 390px, so a phone is offered Day/Month only and a desktop Week preference reads as Day — test asserts gridTemplateColumns '60px 1fr' on a phone, '60px repeat(7, 1fr)' on a desktop.

cd frontend && npm run test -- components/command-center app/command-center → green. → DONE — npm run test -- components/command-center app/command-center → 19 files / 99 tests passed. Full suite 152 files / 786 tests green. (vitest.setup.ts gained a jsdom window.matchMedia shim reporting no-match: hooks/use-mobile calls matchMedia on mount, which is now on the mount path of the CC shell and the calendar. No assertion was changed or removed.)
userStories.notes: cc-stats already steps 6→3 at 1199 and →2 at 700 (globals.css :1621/:1625) — move the 2-up boundary to 768 rather than adding a fourth breakpoint.

userStories.title: Chat compact: one column, sheets for the rest
userStories.description: On a phone the Studio chat is the conversation and nothing else. The three-column .sh-chat-grid becomes one column under 1024; threads move behind the existing left sheet (the classic layout's pattern — reuse it, do not build a second drawer); Auto now stays the pill added in PRD-244 W4 and opens the rail's content in a sheet; the breadcrumb bar (.sh-chat-bar) collapses to the active thread title plus the two controls; the composer is safe-area aware and is never covered by the keyboard.
acceptanceCriteria: Under 1024px .sh-chat-grid is a single column and .sh-chat-threads is not rendered inline; a test asserts the rule and the component behaviour with a mocked width. → DONE — globals.css:2994 (@media max-width: 1023px, compact region) .sh-chat-grid → grid-template-columns: 1fr; studio-chat-shell.tsx:358 the threads aside renders only when `!isCompact && !threadsCollapsed`. Test components/chatbot/__tests__/studio-chat-compact.test.tsx 'compact: nothing but the conversation is in the grid' (width mocked via @/hooks/use-mobile) asserts .sh-chat-grid .sh-chat-threads is absent while .sh-chat-main and the conversation are present; the desktop counterpart asserts the column IS in the grid.

Threads open in a Sheet on narrow viewports, reusing the existing Sheet primitive; no second drawer component is added (grep: no new *-drawer.tsx). → DONE — studio-chat-shell.tsx:204 the list is ONE `threadsPanel` const rendered in either home: the grid aside (:358) or SheetContent side='left' (:380, the existing @/components/ui/sheet). Test 'compact: the bar's toggle opens the same list in a Sheet' clicks the bar control and finds [role=dialog] .sh-chat-threads with its head. 'no second primitive' asserts NO *-drawer.tsx exists in components/chatbot and that {threadsPanel}/{railPanel} each appear exactly twice (two homes, one definition).

The Auto now pill opens the rail's content in a Sheet under 1280px; AutoNowRail itself is unchanged (one rail component, per PRD-244 D5). → DONE — studio-chat-shell.tsx:95-102 reads PRD-244 D5's OWN threshold (AUTO_NOW_RAIL_MIN_WIDTH = 1280, hooks/use-auto-now.ts:17, which globals.css:1270 mirrors by hiding .sh-chat-rail below 1279) — not a third Studio breakpoint; the two compact FORMS still fork at 1024/768. Below it the pill (:198 railShown / :199 toggleRailPanel) opens `railPanel` in SheetContent side='right' (:389); at/above it the grid aside is unchanged. AutoNowRail is untouched and the test asserts exactly ONE rail rendered. The rail sheet has its own open state so a desktop 'rail open' preference cannot auto-open a sheet on a phone (test 'a collapse preference stored on a desktop never opens a sheet on a phone').

The composer carries the safe-area padding from US-001 and the conversation's scroll container accounts for it (no content trapped under the home bar). → DONE — the home-bar inset is reserved EXACTLY ONCE, by .sh-shell.safe-bottom (US-001, main-layout.tsx:96) — the chat's ancestor in the Studio shell, 100dvh + border-box, so the keyboard case also works (dvh shrinks, the composer stays on screen). The two NEW sheets are portals attached to <body>, so they do NOT inherit that padding and carry `safe-bottom` themselves (:380, :389). The composer is NOT given a second inset: chat.tsx's composer is `sticky bottom-0` in the flex column (a sibling of the messages scroll container, which therefore ends above it), so nothing is trapped under it and a second `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` would double the band. Test 'the composer stays in flow, so the conversation never hides under it' asserts all three facts. chat.tsx is shared with Classic and is unmodified.

cd frontend && npm run test -- components/chatbot app/chat → green, including the existing chat-page-resume suite. → DONE — npm run test -- components/chatbot app/chat components/__tests__/studio-mobile-scope.test.ts → 14 files / 62 tests passed, including app/chat/__tests__/chat-page-resume.test.tsx. Full suite 153 files / 795 tests green. components/chatbot/__tests__/auto-now-mounts.test.ts:10 updated for the railPanel extraction (same intent: rail above MissionSection, the bar control is the pill) — it is not one of the six PRD-244 gates and its guarantee is unchanged.
userStories.notes: app/chat/page.tsx already forks on useIsMobile for the history sheet in the CLASSIC layout — that is the pattern to reuse for the Studio shell; do not touch the classic branch.

userStories.title: Assignments hub compact
userStories.description: The hub works one-handed. The entry grid (.entry-grid) is 1-up under 768; the flip tabs (.cc-tabs in the hub) scroll like the Command Centre's; mission and playbook cards stack their meta beneath the title instead of truncating; .status-head wraps. CSS only unless a card's structure genuinely cannot respond.
acceptanceCriteria: Under 768px .entry-grid is one column and the hub's cards stack their meta; rules live in the compact region. → DONE — globals.css:3080 (@media max-width: 767px, compact region) :is(.entry-grid, .mis-cards, .pb-grid) → 1fr, and :3083 .mkt-strip 5-up → 2-up (small promo tiles). Cards stack their meta: :3087 .mis-card .row-meta 4 mono columns → 2, :3092 .pb-card .stats wraps. The two card grids had to become CLASSES first — a media query cannot override an inline style — so missions-body.tsx:274 renders `className="mis-cards"` and playbooks-body.tsx:337 `className="pb-grid"`, with the desktop column counts (2-up / 3-up) beside their card families at globals.css:2525 / :2646. Asserted in studio-mobile-scope.test.ts 'Assignments hub: 1-up entries and cards, stacked meta, a wrapping head' + hub-compact.test.tsx 'the card grids are classes'.

The hub's tab strip scrolls horizontally and keeps its active tab visible, matching the Command Centre's behaviour from US-002. → DONE — assignments-hub.tsx:19/:55/:103 uses the SAME hooks/use-tab-strip-scroll.ts the Command Centre uses (US-002) — one hook, not a copy; the scope gate asserts both files import it. Test components/assignments/__tests__/hub-compact.test.tsx 'scrolls the active tab into view on a compact viewport' (?tab=missions, width mocked) and the desktop counterpart. The strip's bleed/gutter fix from US-002 (globals.css:3021-3022) is shared too — the hub's root is .cc-page.

.status-head wraps rather than truncating under 768px, and remains in the chrome guard. → DONE — globals.css:3094 .status-head { flex-wrap: wrap } under 767px, so the label, count and right-hand control wrap instead of squeezing. It is untouched in the chrome guard (globals.css:2868, still listing .status-head with flex-shrink: 0) and page-frames.test.ts is green.

cd frontend && npm run test -- components/assignments app/assignments → green. → DONE — npm run test -- components/assignments app/assignments → 2 files / 11 tests passed. Full suite 154 files / 803 tests green. Beyond the ACs, the story's 'works one-handed' also needed the DEFAULT Missions view: GroupedView renders .mis-row, a 7-column ledger 644px wide at its narrowest, so globals.css:3102-3110 gives it a two-line phone form (pip · id · age, then the goal and sub across the row) and drops the three figures the sub-line already covers; and both 7-column ledger views (missions Table, playbooks List/act-table) are now desktop-only like the Command Centre's activity table (missions-body.tsx:93, playbooks-body.tsx:58) — tested both widths.
userStories.notes: The hub's root is .cc-page and its rules hang off :is(.studio, .cc-page) — keep that scoping; a bare .entry-grid rule would leak into Classic.

userStories.title: Agents, Deliverables and Tools compact
userStories.description: The three bespoke Studio pages read on a phone: their in-page .cc-tabs scroll (US-002's behaviour), .cc-stats is 2-up (US-001/US-002's rule covers it — verify, do not duplicate), roster and marketplace cards are 1-up, and .cc-toolbar wraps its search, pills and segmented controls rather than overflowing.
acceptanceCriteria: Under 768px the roster grid, the deliverables cards and the tools application grid are one column.
.cc-toolbar wraps under 768px with its controls full-width where sensible; no horizontal overflow at 390px on any of the three pages.
The three pages' tab strips scroll and keep the active tab visible (shared behaviour, not three copies).
cd frontend && npm run test -- components/agents components/deliverables components/tools → green.
userStories.notes: Tools is a frame variant inside a 1,035-line component (ToolsDashboard variant='studio') — change the frame's CSS, not the shared grid or modals.

userStories.title: The framed pages, in one move
userStories.description: PageHeader, StatsBar and FilterTabs get compact forms, which converts every page built on them at once: Team, Analytics, Settings and its sub-pages, Knowledge Base, Marketplace and its sub-pages, mission detail, and the three admin surfaces. In Studio: the head's eyebrow/title/lede stack with actions below, StatsBar is 2-up, FilterTabs scrolls. Classic's render is untouched in both forms.
acceptanceCriteria: Under 768px the Studio PageHeader stacks its actions beneath the head; StatsBar's cc-stats form is 2-up; the Studio FilterTabs strip scrolls with its active tab visible.
The Classic branches of all three primitives are byte-unchanged (a test asserts the classic markup still renders the gradient title, the card grid and the Radix tablist).
A test renders each primitive at a mocked narrow width in the Studio style and asserts the compact structure.
cd frontend && npm run test -- components/shared → green, including the studio-frame-primitives suite.
userStories.notes: These three primitives are the leverage that converted 24/11/9 pages in PRD-244 W5d-g — a change here reaches every framed page, so keep it conservative and test both branches.

userStories.title: The route forks flip to the style axis
userStories.description: With every Studio surface compact, the six routes stop choosing a COMPONENT by width: app/chat, app/command-center, app/assignments, app/agents, app/deliverables and app/tools render the Studio component whenever the style is Studio, at any width, and the classic component whenever the style is Classic. Width now only informs layout INSIDE a component. Classic components stay exactly where they are (PRD-246 M6) and no file is deleted.
acceptanceCriteria: All six routes fork on isStudio alone; useIsTabletOrBelow no longer selects between components in any of them (grep: no 'isStudio && !is' pattern left in app/**/page.tsx).
Each route's test asserts: Studio style at phone width renders the Studio component; Classic style at any width renders the classic component.
No classic component is deleted or unmounted — /missions and /playbooks redirects keep working at every width.
cd frontend && npm run test -- app → green.
userStories.notes: This story is LAST for a reason: flipping it before US-002..006 would put a desktop-shaped Studio on every phone. If any earlier story is un-DONE, do not start this one.

userStories.title: Gates and the pass checklist
userStories.description: Lock the work in. A mobile scope gate asserts every Studio class family that renders on a phone has compact rules in the compact region; the route tests from US-007 are the behavioural gate; and the manual checklist in the PRD's tail is the human gate. Do not weaken any PRD-244 gate to make these pass.
acceptanceCriteria: A new test (e.g. components/__tests__/studio-mobile-scope.test.ts) asserts the compact region exists and covers each family: sh-chat, cc-tabs, cc-stats, entry-grid, the card families and the toolbar.
The PRD-244 gates all still pass unchanged: prd244-w0-honesty, studio-honest-chrome, cc-page-scope, studio-surfaces-scope, markdown-typography, page-frames.
bash scripts/ralph/acceptance-prd246.sh exits 0.
cd frontend && npm run test → the full frontend suite is green.
userStories.notes: If a PRD-244 gate genuinely contradicts a mobile requirement, RALPH_BLOCKED with the grep — never edit a gate to make a story pass.
